chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I instructed a man to ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on my behalf about a man who caught fish while they were alive, then took them out after some of them had died. He said: 'That which died, do not eat it, for it died in what contains its life, and this report does not contradict this.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish that died in the water?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on fish that perish while still submerged, declaring them impure because they died in their natural element of life. This establishes the foundational Shia juristic principle that aquatic creatures must be slaughtered by being removed from water while alive to be considered halal, distinguishing them from those that die naturally in the water.
